name: Terence Tao
milestone_by_age_26: Became a full professor of mathematics at UCLA at age 24, having already earned a PhD from Princeton at 20 and won IMO gold at 13.
early_history_summary: A child prodigy from Adelaide, Australia, Tao taught himself to read at age 2 and began university-level mathematics at age 9. He won IMO bronze, silver, and gold medals at ages 10-13, becoming the youngest IMO gold medalist in history. He completed his BSc at Flinders University by 16, earned his PhD from Princeton at 20, and joined UCLA's faculty immediately, achieving full professorship at 24.
family_context_summary: Born to Billy Tao, a Chinese-born pediatrician, and Grace Tao, who held a degree in physics and mathematics from the University of Hong Kong. Both parents emigrated from Hong Kong to Australia in 1972. His two younger brothers also earned PhDs.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a pediatrician who researched gifted education; mother was a physics and mathematics graduate who taught secondary school. Both parents actively designed individualized educational programs for Terry from a young age.
evidence_summary: Terence Tao exhibited extraordinary mathematical ability from toddlerhood, teaching himself to read at 2 and mastering university-level math by 9. His parents, both university-educated in technical fields, designed a highly individualized educational program with Flinders University and secondary schools. He won IMO gold at 13, completed his BSc at Flinders by 16, earned a PhD from Princeton at 20, and became a full professor at UCLA at 24 — all before his 26th birthday. His father's research on gifted education directly informed the educational acceleration strategy.
starting_point: Born in 1975 in Adelaide, Australia to Chinese immigrant parents; father was a pediatrician and mother a physics/mathematics graduate who taught secondary school.
current_position: Professor of mathematics at UCLA holding the James and Carol Collins Chair; Fields Medalist (2006), Breakthrough Prize winner (2014), widely regarded as one of the greatest living mathematicians.

He entered Dalhousie University at 12, completed his bachelor's at 14, and earned his PhD from the University of Waterloo at 20 on computational origami. He immediately joined MIT's faculty, becoming the youngest professor in MIT history.

name: Peter Scholze
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest professor of mathematics in Germany at age 24 (2012) after revolutionizing arithmetic geometry by introducing perfectoid spaces in his PhD thesis.
early_history_summary: Born in Dresden and raised in Berlin, Scholze taught himself college-level mathematics at 14 while attending a math-science gymnasium. He won three gold medals and one silver at the IMO. At the University of Bonn, he completed his bachelor's in three semesters and master's in two more. At 22, he rewrote a 288-page proof from a key number theory book into just 37 pages, stunning the mathematical community. He completed his PhD on perfectoid spaces in 2011 and was appointed full professor at Bonn in 2012 at age 24.
family_context_summary: Born in Dresden, East Germany; father is a physicist and mother is a computer scientist. His sister studied chemistry. The family provided a scientifically oriented household.

His PhD thesis introducing perfectoid spaces (2011) revolutionized arithmetic geometry, and he became Germany's youngest mathematics professor at 24. His parents' scientific backgrounds provided a supportive home environment.

He became a full tenured professor at Harvard at 26, the youngest in the university's history.
